opener_episode.title: Hala Taha: How to Turn Social Media Visibility Into a Revenue Engine
opener_episode.why: Hala's own newest episode is about turning social attention into revenue, which is the core of Avery's 'Click & Mortar' model (social-first marketing plus curated pop-ups) that took ArtLife.com to an eight-figure-a-year business, and of how he built Alec Monopoly into a global brand. Referencing the host's own episode lands with a host who personally picks guests. Guest-episode alternative: Haley Sacks (2026-10-05) on status spending.

angles.headline: Click & Mortar: turning Instagram attention into eight-figure art sales
angles.pitch: How Avery used social-first marketing plus curated physical pop-ups to scale ArtLife.com (launched 2015) into an eight-figure-a-year business - a model since widely copied.
angles.builds_on: Hala's 'Social Media Visibility Into a Revenue Engine' (2026-10-02)

angles.headline: Personal branding masterclass: building Alec Monopoly into a global brand
angles.pitch: A framework-driven breakdown of how Avery developed a street artist into a global brand with sold-out shows from New York to Morocco and major brand partnerships.

angles.headline: Selling to the ultra-wealthy: the psychology of luxury buyers
angles.pitch: What advising celebrities, athletes and HNW collectors (e.g. placing a $100K+ Hap Tivey work with Kris Jenner at Art Basel Miami Beach 2024) teaches about selling high-ticket items.
angles.builds_on: Shelby Haas-Sapp sales psychology (2026-09-30) and Haley Sacks on status spending (2026-10-05)
